chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about al-qasāmah: where did it begin? He said: “It was from the time of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. After the conquest of Khaybar, a man from the Anṣār fell behind his companions. They went back searching for him and found him rolling in his blood, slain. The Anṣār came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said: O Messenger of Allah, the Jews killed our companion. He said: Let fifty men from among you swear that they killed him.” They said: O Messenger of Allah, shall we swear to what we did not see? He said: “Then let the Jews swear.” They said: O Messenger of Allah, and who would believe the Jews? So he said: “Then I shall pay for your companion.”

So I said to him: How is the ruling in it? He said: “Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ruled concerning bloodshed in a manner unlike what He has ruled in any other matter among the rights of the people, because of His magnification of blood. If a man were to claim against another man ten thousand dirhams, or less or more, the oath would not be upon the claimant; rather, the oath would be upon the one claimed against. But when a man claims against a group that they killed, then the oath belongs to the claimant of blood before those claimed against. So the claimant must bring fifty who swear that so-and-so killed so-and-so, then the one sworn against is handed over to them. If they wish, they may pardon; and if they wish, they may accept the diyah. If they do not swear, then those against whom the claim was made must have fifty of them swear: We did not kill him, nor do we know any killer for him. If they do that, then the people of the village in which he was found must pay; and if he was in an open land, his diyah is paid from the Bayt al-Māl of the Muslims.”
For Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to say: “The blood of a Muslim man is not left unavenged or uncompensated.”

key_terms.الدِّمَاءِ: Bloodshed or cases involving human life, treated with special legal gravity.
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: Blood-money paid as financial compensation for a killing.
key_terms.الْقَسَامَةِ: The procedure of multiple sworn oaths used in homicide cases when decisive proof is lacking.
key_terms.الْمُدَّعَى عَلَيْهِ: The person or group against whom the legal claim is made.
key_terms.الْمُدَّعِي: The claimant who brings a legal accusation.
key_terms.الْيَمِينُ: A formal oath used as legal proof in judicial proceedings.
key_terms.بَيْتِ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: The public treasury of the Muslims, which bears liability in certain unresolved cases.

ai.seo_question: How does al-qasāmah work in Shia hadith law for unresolved murder cases?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the origin and legal framework of al-qasāmah in cases of suspected murder, tracing it back to a judgment of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله after Khaybar. It emphasizes the grave sanctity of bloodshed in Islamic law and sets out how oaths, liability, diyah, and public treasury responsibility apply when a killer is not conclusively identified.
